title: LOCKED ASYMMETRY: manifest `pattern` absence is lenient in C++, strict in Python

py_load_manifest.error_substring: is not a supported plugin family

why: This is a locked absence asymmetry: this
manifest has NO `pattern` key at all. C++ (neither registry dispatches on
`pattern` — binding is driven entirely by arg_spec) is LENIENT about its
absence and proceeds past that gate. Python's `load_manifest` NEEDS a
pattern to pick a Loaded* class (`loaders = {"vector": ..., "pure": ...}`,
`if pattern not in loaders: raise`), so it is STRICT.
Both outcomes here are REJECT, but for DIFFERENT reasons, proven with zero
GPU/dlopen: the manifest is deliberately ALSO malformed (a duplicate plugin
id). C++, having passed the lenient pattern gate, reaches the pre-existing
duplicate-id structural check and rejects THERE. Python's strict pattern
gate fires first and never reaches the duplicate-id check.
The top-level expect/substring is C++'s outcome (the default); the
`py_load_manifest` override is Python's — the override IS the asymmetry,
made mechanical instead of a locked-but-latent inspection finding.
